sources.finding: New Zealand soldiers were called Kiwis by 1917, during the war.
Kiwi can be seen in daylight; strictly night-only is inaccurate.
Kiwi eggs typically weigh 15-20 percent of female body mass; five species are recognised.
There are five species, all requiring conservation rather than a single species.
Jack Turner proposed the commercial name in Auckland in June 1959; the fruit section is consistent with the US export context.
